# indicatif - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/indicatif/^0.18/

## Expand description

indicatif is a library for Rust that helps you build command line interfaces that report progress to users. It comes with various tools and utilities for formatting anything that indicates progress.

Platform support:

- Linux
- macOS
- Windows (colors require Windows 10)

Best paired with other libraries in the family:

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-contents)Crate Contents

- **Progress bars**- `ProgressBar`
- `MultiProgress`

- **Data Formatting**- `HumanBytes`
- `DecimalBytes`
- `BinaryBytes`
- `HumanDuration`
- `HumanCount`
- `HumanFloatCount`

[§](https://docs.rs#progress-bars-and-spinners)Progress Bars and Spinners

indicatif comes with a [ ProgressBar](https://docs.rs/struct.ProgressBar.html) type that supports both bounded
progress bar uses as well as unbounded “spinner” type progress reports.
Progress bars are

[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)

`Sync`[objects which means that they are internally locked and can be passed from thread to thread.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html)

`Send`Additionally a [ MultiProgress](https://docs.rs/struct.MultiProgress.html) utility is provided that can manage
rendering multiple progress bars at once (eg: from multiple threads).

To whet your appetite, this is what this can look like:

Progress bars are manually advanced and by default draw to stderr. When you are done, the progress bar can be finished either visibly (eg: the progress bar stays on the screen) or cleared (the progress bar will be removed).

```
use indicatif::ProgressBar;
let bar = ProgressBar::new(1000);
for _ in 0..1000 {
    bar.inc(1);
    // ...
}
bar.finish();
```
Spinners can be manually advanced with [ tick](https://docs.rs/struct.ProgressBar.html#method.tick), or you can set them up
to spin automatically with

[:](https://docs.rs/struct.ProgressBar.html#method.enable_steady_tick)

`enable_steady_tick````
use std::time::Duration;
use indicatif::ProgressBar;
let bar = ProgressBar::new_spinner();
bar.enable_steady_tick(Duration::from_millis(100));
// ... do some work
bar.finish();
```
General progress bar behaviors:

- if a non terminal is detected the progress bar will be completely hidden. This makes piping programs to logfiles make sense out of the box.
- a progress bar only starts drawing when `set_message``inc``set_position``tick``tick`
- progress bars should be explicitly finished to reset the rendering for others. Either by also clearing them or by replacing them with a new message / retaining the current message.
- the default template renders neither message nor prefix.

[§](https://docs.rs#iterators)Iterators

Similar to [tqdm](https://github.com/tqdm/tqdm), progress bars can be
associated with an iterator. For example:

```
use indicatif::ProgressIterator;
for _ in (0..1000).progress() {
    // ...
}
```
See the [ ProgressIterator](https://docs.rs/trait.ProgressIterator.html) trait for more
methods to configure the number of elements in the iterator or change
the progress bar style. Indicatif also has optional support for parallel
iterators with

[Rayon](https://github.com/rayon-rs/rayon). In your

`Cargo.toml`, use the “rayon” feature:```
[dependencies]
indicatif = {version = "*", features = ["rayon"]}
```
And then use it like this:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use indicatif::ParallelProgressIterator;
use rayon::iter::{ParallelIterator, IntoParallelRefIterator};
let v: Vec<_> = (0..100000).collect();
let v2: Vec<_> = v.par_iter().progress_count(v.len() as u64).map(|i| i + 1).collect();
assert_eq!(v2[0], 1);
```
Or if you’d like to customize the progress bar:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use indicatif::{ProgressBar, ParallelProgressIterator, ProgressStyle};
use rayon::iter::{ParallelIterator, IntoParallelRefIterator};
// Alternatively, use `ProgressBar::new().with_style()`
let style = ProgressStyle::default_bar();
let v: Vec<_> = (0..100000).collect();
let v2: Vec<_> = v.par_iter().progress_with_style(style).map(|i| i + 1).collect();
assert_eq!(v2[0], 1);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#templates)Templates

Progress bars can be styled with simple format strings similar to the
ones in Rust itself.  The format for a placeholder is `{key:options}`
where the `options` part is optional.  If provided the format is this:

```
<^>             for an optional alignment specification (left, center and right respectively)
WIDTH           an optional width as positive integer
!               an optional exclamation mark to enable truncation
.STYLE          an optional dot separated style string
/STYLE          an optional dot separated alternative style string
```
For the style component see [ Style::from_dotted_str](https://docs.rs/console/0.7.5/console/struct.Style.html#method.from_dotted_str)
for more information. Indicatif uses the

`console` base crate for all
colorization and formatting options.Some examples for templates:

`[{elapsed_precise}] {bar:40.cyan/blue} {pos:>7}/{len:7} {msg}`This sets a progress bar that is 40 characters wide and has cyan as primary style color and blue as alternative style color. Alternative styles are currently only used for progress bars.

Example configuration:

```
bar.set_style(ProgressStyle::with_template("[{elapsed_precise}] {bar:40.cyan/blue} {pos:>7}/{len:7} {msg}")
    .unwrap()
    .progress_chars("##-"));
```
The following keys exist:

- `bar`: renders a progress bar. By default 20 characters wide. The style string is used to color the elapsed part, the alternative style is used for the bar that is yet to render.
- `wide_bar`: like- `bar`but always fills the remaining space. It should not be used with- `wide_msg`.
- `spinner`: renders the spinner (current tick string). Note that spinners do not automatically tick by default. You either need to call- `enable_steady_tick`or manually call- `tick`.
- `prefix`: renders the prefix set on the progress bar.
- `msg`: renders the currently set message on the progress bar.
- `wide_msg`: like- `msg`but always fills the remaining space and truncates. It should not be used with- `wide_bar`.
- `pos`: renders the current position of the bar as integer
- `human_pos`: renders the current position of the bar as an integer, with commas as the thousands separator.
- `len`: renders the amount of work to be done as an integer
- `human_len`: renders the total length of the bar as an integer, with commas as the thousands separator.
- `percent`: renders the current position of the bar as a percentage of the total length (as an integer).
- `percent_precise`: renders the current position of the bar as a percentage of the total length (with 3 fraction digits).
- `bytes`: renders the current position of the bar as bytes (alias of- `binary_bytes`).
- `total_bytes`: renders the total length of the bar as bytes (alias of- `binary_total_bytes`).
- `decimal_bytes`: renders the current position of the bar as bytes using power-of-10 units, i.e.- `MB`,- `kB`, etc.
- `decimal_total_bytes`: renders the total length of the bar as bytes using power-of-10 units, i.e.- `MB`,- `kB`, etc.
- `binary_bytes`: renders the current position of the bar as bytes using power-of-two units, i.e.- `MiB`,- `KiB`, etc.
- `binary_total_bytes`: renders the total length of the bar as bytes using power-of-two units, i.e.- `MiB`,- `KiB`, etc.
- `elapsed_precise`: renders the elapsed time as- `HH:MM:SS`.
- `elapsed`: renders the elapsed time as- `42s`,- `1m`etc.
- `per_sec`: renders the speed in steps per second.
- `bytes_per_sec`: renders the speed in bytes per second (alias of- `binary_bytes_per_sec`).
- `decimal_bytes_per_sec`: renders the speed in bytes per second using power-of-10 units, i.e.- `MB`,- `kB`, etc.
- `binary_bytes_per_sec`: renders the speed in bytes per second using power-of-two units, i.e.- `MiB`,- `KiB`, etc.
- `eta_precise`: the remaining time (like- `elapsed_precise`).
- `eta`: the remaining time (like- `elapsed`).
- `duration_precise`: the extrapolated total duration (like- `elapsed_precise`).
- `duration`: the extrapolated total duration time (like- `elapsed`).

If the list above does not contain the value you need, consider creating a custom
[ ProgressTracker](https://docs.rs/style/trait.ProgressTracker.html) implementation.

The design of the progress bar can be altered with the integrated
template functionality.  The template can be set by changing a
[ ProgressStyle](https://docs.rs/style/struct.ProgressStyle.html) and attaching it to the progress bar.

[§](https://docs.rs#human-readable-formatting)Human Readable Formatting

There are some formatting wrappers for showing elapsed time and file sizes for human users:

```
use indicatif::{HumanBytes, HumanCount, HumanDuration, HumanFloatCount};
assert_eq!("3.00 MiB", HumanBytes(3*1024*1024).to_string());
assert_eq!("8 seconds", HumanDuration(Duration::from_secs(8)).to_string());
assert_eq!("33,857,009", HumanCount(33857009).to_string());
assert_eq!("33,857,009.1235", HumanFloatCount(33857009.123456).to_string());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

- `rayon`: adds rayon support
- `improved_unicode`: adds improved unicode support (graphemes, better width calculation)

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::style::`- [ProgressStyle](https://docs.rs/style/struct.ProgressStyle.html);

# sha1 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sha1/^0.10/

## Expand description

Pure Rust implementation of the [SHA-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-1) cryptographic hash algorithm
with optional hardware-specific optimizations.

[§](https://docs.rs#-warning-cryptographically-broken-)🚨 Warning: Cryptographically Broken! 🚨

The SHA-1 hash function should be considered cryptographically broken and
unsuitable for further use in any security critical capacity, as it is
[practically vulnerable to chosen-prefix collisions](https://sha-mbles.github.io/).

We provide this crate for legacy interoperability purposes only.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use hex_literal::hex;
use sha1::{Sha1, Digest};
// create a Sha1 object
let mut hasher = Sha1::new();
// process input message
hasher.update(b"hello world");
// acquire hash digest in the form of GenericArray,
// which in this case is equivalent to [u8; 20]
let result = hasher.finalize();
assert_eq!(result[..], hex!("2aae6c35c94fcfb415dbe95f408b9ce91ee846ed"));
```
Also see [RustCrypto/hashes](https://github.com/RustCrypto/hashes) readme.

[§](https://docs.rs#note-for-users-of-sha1-v06)Note for users of `sha1 v0.6`

This crate has been transferred to the RustCrypto organization and uses
implementation previously published as the `sha-1` crate. The previous
zero dependencies version is now published as the [ sha1_smol](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/sha1-smol/) crate.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [digest](https://docs.rs/digest/0.10.7/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/digest/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Sha1](https://docs.rs/struct.Sha1Core.html)- Core
- Core SHA-1 hasher state.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Digest](https://docs.rs/trait.Digest.html)
- Convenience wrapper trait covering functionality of cryptographic hash functions with fixed output size.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- SHA-1 compression function

# tracing_subscriber - Rust

## Expand description

Utilities for implementing and composing [ tracing](https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing) subscribers.

[ tracing](https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing) is a framework for instrumenting Rust programs to collect
scoped, structured, and async-aware diagnostics. The

[trait represents the functionality necessary to collect this trace data. This crate contains tools for composing subscribers out of smaller units of behaviour, and batteries-included implementations of common subscriber functionality.](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.35/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html)

`Subscriber``tracing-subscriber` is intended for use by both `Subscriber` authors and
application authors using `tracing` to instrument their applications.

*Compiler support:  requires *

`rustc` 1.65+[§](https://docs.rs#layers-and-filters)`Layer`s and `Filter`s

The most important component of the `tracing-subscriber` API is the
[ Layer](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html) trait, which provides a composable abstraction for building

[s. Like the](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.35/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html)

`Subscriber`[trait, a](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.35/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html)

`Subscriber`[defines a particular behavior for collecting trace data. Unlike](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[s, which implement a](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.35/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html)

`Subscriber`*complete*strategy for how trace data is collected,

[s provide](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`*modular*implementations of specific behaviors. Therefore, they can be

[composed together](https://docs.rs/layer/index.html#composing-layers)to form a

[which is capable of recording traces in a variety of ways. See the](https://docs.rs/tracing-core/0.1.35/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing_core/subscriber/trait.Subscriber.html)

`Subscriber`[for details on using](https://docs.rs/layer/index.html)

`layer` module’s
documentation[s.](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`In addition, the [ Filter](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Filter.html) trait defines an interface for filtering what
spans and events are recorded by a particular layer. This allows different

[s to handle separate subsets of the trace data emitted by a program. See the](https://docs.rs/layer/trait.Layer.html)

`Layer`[documentation on per-layer filtering](https://docs.rs/layer/index.html#per-layer-filtering)for more information on using

[§](https://docs.rs#supported-rust-versions)Supported Rust Versions

Tracing is built against the latest stable release. The minimum supported version is 1.65. The current Tracing version is not guaranteed to build on Rust versions earlier than the minimum supported version.

Tracing follows the same compiler support policies as the rest of the Tokio project. The current stable Rust compiler and the three most recent minor versions before it will always be supported. For example, if the current stable compiler version is 1.69, the minimum supported version will not be increased past 1.66, three minor versions prior. Increasing the minimum supported compiler version is not considered a semver breaking change as long as doing so complies with this policy.

# ureq - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ureq/^2.10/

## Expand description

A simple, safe HTTP client.

[!NOTE]

- 2.12.x is MSRV 1.71
- 2.11.x is MSRV 1.67
For both these lines, we will release patch version pinning dependencies as needed to retain the MSRV. If we are bumping MSRV, that will require a minor version bump.

[!NOTE] ureq version 2.11.0 was forced to bump MSRV from 1.63 -> 1.67. The problem is that the

`time`crate 0.3.20, the last 1.63 compatible version, stopped compiling with Rust[1.80 and above](https://github.com/algesten/ureq/pull/878#issuecomment-2503176155). To release a 2.x version that is possible to compile on the latest Rust we were forced to bump MSRV.

Ureq’s first priority is being easy for you to use. It’s great for
anyone who wants a low-overhead HTTP client that just gets the job done. Works
very well with HTTP APIs. Its features include cookies, JSON, HTTP proxies,
HTTPS, interoperability with the `http` crate, and charset decoding.

Ureq is in pure Rust for safety and ease of understanding. It avoids using
`unsafe` directly. It [uses blocking I/O](https://docs.rs#blocking-io-for-simplicity) instead of async I/O, because that keeps
the API simple and keeps dependencies to a minimum. For TLS, ureq uses
[rustls or native-tls](https://docs.rs#https--tls--ssl).

See the [changelog](https://github.com/algesten/ureq/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for details of recent releases.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

In its simplest form, ureq looks like this:

```
fn main() -> Result<(), ureq::Error> {
    let body: String = ureq::get("http://example.com")
        .set("Example-Header", "header value")
        .call()?
        .into_string()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
For more involved tasks, you’ll want to create an [Agent](https://docs.rs/struct.Agent.html). An Agent
holds a connection pool for reuse, and a cookie store if you use the
“cookies” feature. An Agent can be cheaply cloned due to an internal
[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html) and all clones of an Agent share state among each other. Creating
an Agent also allows setting options like the TLS configuration.

```
  use ureq::{Agent, AgentBuilder};
  use std::time::Duration;
  let agent: Agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
      .timeout_read(Duration::from_secs(5))
      .timeout_write(Duration::from_secs(5))
      .build();
  let body: String = agent.get("http://example.com/page")
      .call()?
      .into_string()?;
  // Reuses the connection from previous request.
  let response: String = agent.put("http://example.com/upload")
      .set("Authorization", "example-token")
      .call()?
      .into_string()?;
```
Ureq supports sending and receiving json, if you enable the “json” feature:

```
  // Requires the `json` feature enabled.
  let resp: String = ureq::post("http://myapi.example.com/post/ingest")
      .set("X-My-Header", "Secret")
      .send_json(ureq::json!({
          "name": "martin",
          "rust": true
      }))?
      .into_string()?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#error-handling)Error handling

ureq returns errors via `Result<T, ureq::Error>`. That includes I/O errors,
protocol errors, and status code errors (when the server responded 4xx or
5xx)

```
use ureq::Error;
match ureq::get("http://mypage.example.com/").call() {
    Ok(response) => { /* it worked */},
    Err(Error::Status(code, response)) => {
        /* the server returned an unexpected status
           code (such as 400, 500 etc) */
    }
    Err(_) => { /* some kind of io/transport error */ }
}
```
More details on the [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html) type.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

To enable a minimal dependency tree, some features are off by default. You can control them when including ureq as a dependency.

`ureq = { version = "*", features = ["json", "charset"] }`

- `tls`enables https. This is enabled by default.
- `native-certs`makes the default TLS implementation use the OS’ trust store (see TLS doc below).
- `cookies`enables cookies.
- `json`enables- [Response::into_json()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.into_json)and- [Request::send_json()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_json)via serde_json.
- `charset`enables interpreting the charset part of the Content-Type header (e.g.- `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=iso-8859-1`). Without this, the library defaults to Rust’s built in- `utf-8`.
- `socks-proxy`enables proxy config using the- `socks4://`,- `socks4a://`,- `socks5://`and- `socks://`(equal to- `socks5://`) prefix.
- `native-tls`enables an adapter so you can pass a- `native_tls::TlsConnector`instance to- `AgentBuilder::tls_connector`. Due to the risk of diamond dependencies accidentally switching on an unwanted TLS implementation,- `native-tls`is never picked up as a default or used by the crate level convenience calls (- `ureq::get`etc) – it must be configured on the agent. The- `native-certs`feature does nothing for- `native-tls`.
- `gzip`enables requests of gzip-compressed responses and decompresses them. This is enabled by default.
- `brotli`enables requests brotli-compressed responses and decompresses them.
- `http-interop`enables conversion methods to and from- `http::Response`and- `http::request::Builder`(v0.2).
- `http`enables conversion methods to and from- `http::Response`and- `http::request::Builder`(v1.0).

[§](https://docs.rs#plain-requests)Plain requests

Most standard methods (GET, POST, PUT etc), are supported as functions from the
top of the library ([get()](https://docs.rs/fn.get.html), [post()](https://docs.rs/fn.post.html), [put()](https://docs.rs/fn.put.html), etc).

These top level http method functions create a [Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html) instance
which follows a build pattern. The builders are finished using:

- `.call()`
- `.send()`- [Read](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)(chunked encoding support for non-known sized readers).
- `.send_string()`
- `.send_bytes()`
- `.send_form()`

[§](https://docs.rs#json)JSON

By enabling the `ureq = { version = "*", features = ["json"] }` feature,
the library supports serde json.

- `request.send_json()`
- `response.into_json()`

[§](https://docs.rs#content-length-and-transfer-encoding)Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding

The library will send a Content-Length header on requests with bodies of
known size, in other words, those sent with
[ .send_string()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_string),

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_bytes)

`.send_bytes()`[, or](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_form)

`.send_form()`[. If you send a request body with](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_json)

`.send_json()`[, which takes a](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send)

`.send()`[Read](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)of unknown size, ureq will send Transfer-Encoding: chunked, and encode the body accordingly. Bodyless requests (GETs and HEADs) are sent with

[and ureq adds neither a Content-Length nor a Transfer-Encoding header.](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.call)

`.call()`If you set your own Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding header before sending the body, ureq will respect that header by not overriding it, and by encoding the body or not, as indicated by the headers you set.

```
let resp = ureq::post("http://my-server.com/ingest")
    .set("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")
    .send_string("Hello world");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#character-encoding)Character encoding

By enabling the `ureq = { version = "*", features = ["charset"] }` feature,
the library supports sending/receiving other character sets than `utf-8`.

For [ response.into_string()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.into_string) we read the
header

`Content-Type: text/plain; charset=iso-8859-1` and if it contains a charset
specification, we try to decode the body using that encoding. In the absence of, or failing
to interpret the charset, we fall back on `utf-8`.Similarly when using [ request.send_string()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_string),
we first check if the user has set a

`; charset=<whatwg charset>` and attempt
to encode the request body using that.[§](https://docs.rs#proxying)Proxying

ureq supports two kinds of proxies,  [ HTTP](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Proxy_servers_and_tunneling#http_tunneling) (

[),](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/CONNECT)

`CONNECT`[and](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SOCKS#SOCKS4)

`SOCKS4`[, the former is always available while the latter must be enabled using the feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SOCKS#SOCKS5)

`SOCKS5``ureq = { version = "*", features = ["socks-proxy"] }`.Proxies settings are configured on an [Agent](https://docs.rs/struct.Agent.html) (using [AgentBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentBuilder.html)). All request sent
through the agent will be proxied.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-using-http)Example using HTTP

```
fn proxy_example_1() -> std::result::Result<(), ureq::Error> {
    // Configure an http connect proxy. Notice we could have used
    // the http:// prefix here (it's optional).
    let proxy = ureq::Proxy::new("user:password@cool.proxy:9090")?;
    let agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
        .proxy(proxy)
        .build();
    // This is proxied.
    let resp = agent.get("http://cool.server").call()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-using-socks5)Example using SOCKS5

```
fn proxy_example_2() -> std::result::Result<(), ureq::Error> {
    // Configure a SOCKS proxy.
    let proxy = ureq::Proxy::new("socks5://user:password@cool.proxy:9090")?;
    let agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
        .proxy(proxy)
        .build();
    // This is proxied.
    let resp = agent.get("http://cool.server").call()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#https--tls--ssl)HTTPS / TLS / SSL

On platforms that support rustls, ureq uses rustls. On other platforms, native-tls can
be manually configured using [ AgentBuilder::tls_connector](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentBuilder.html#method.tls_connector).

You might want to use native-tls if you need to interoperate with servers that only support less-secure TLS configurations (rustls doesn’t support TLS 1.0 and 1.1, for instance). You might also want to use it if you need to validate certificates for IP addresses, which are not currently supported in rustls.

Here’s an example of constructing an Agent that uses native-tls. It requires the “native-tls” feature to be enabled.

```
  use std::sync::Arc;
  use ureq::Agent;
  let agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
      .tls_connector(Arc::new(native_tls::TlsConnector::new()?))
      .build();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#trusted-roots)Trusted Roots

When you use rustls (`tls` feature), ureq defaults to trusting
[webpki-roots](https://docs.rs/webpki-roots/), a
copy of the Mozilla Root program that is bundled into your program (and so won’t update if your
program isn’t updated). You can alternately configure
[rustls-native-certs](https://docs.rs/rustls-native-certs/) which extracts the roots from your
OS’ trust store. That means it will update when your OS is updated, and also that it will
include locally installed roots.

When you use `native-tls`, ureq will use your OS’ certificate verifier and root store.

[§](https://docs.rs#blocking-io-for-simplicity)Blocking I/O for simplicity

Ureq uses blocking I/O rather than Rust’s newer [asynchronous (async) I/O](https://rust-lang.github.io/async-book/01_getting_started/02_why_async.html). Async I/O
allows serving many concurrent requests without high costs in memory and OS threads. But
it comes at a cost in complexity. Async programs need to pull in a runtime (usually
[async-std](https://github.com/async-rs/async-std#async-std) or [tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio#tokio)). They also need async variants of any method that might block, and of
[any method that might call another method that might block](https://journal.stuffwithstuff.com/2015/02/01/what-color-is-your-function/). That means async
programs usually have a lot of dependencies - which adds to compile times, and increases
risk.

The costs of async are worth paying, if you’re writing an HTTP server that must serve
many many clients with minimal overhead. However, for HTTP *clients*, we believe that the
cost is usually not worth paying. The low-cost alternative to async I/O is blocking I/O,
which has a different price: it requires an OS thread per concurrent request. However,
that price is usually not high: most HTTP clients make requests sequentially, or with
low concurrency.

That’s why ureq uses blocking I/O and plans to stay that way. Other HTTP clients offer both an async API and a blocking API, but we want to offer a blocking API without pulling in all the dependencies required by an async API.

Ureq is inspired by other great HTTP clients like
[superagent](http://visionmedia.github.io/superagent/) and
[the fetch API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API).

If ureq is not what you’re looking for, check out these other Rust HTTP clients:
[surf](https://crates.io/crates/surf), [reqwest](https://crates.io/crates/reqwest),
[isahc](https://crates.io/crates/isahc), [attohttpc](https://crates.io/crates/attohttpc),
[actix-web](https://crates.io/crates/actix-web), and [hyper](https://crates.io/crates/hyper).

# oxidize_pdf - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/target-redirect/oxidize_pdf/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#oxidize-pdf)oxidize-pdf

A comprehensive, pure Rust PDF library for generation, parsing, and manipulation with zero external PDF dependencies.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- **PDF Generation**: Create multi-page documents with text, graphics, and images
- **PDF Parsing**: Complete parser supporting rendering and content extraction
- **PDF Operations**: Split, merge, rotate, and extract pages
- **Text Extraction**: Extract text with position and formatting information
- **Image Extraction**: Extract images in JPEG, PNG, and TIFF formats
- **Font Embedding**: TrueType and OpenType font embedding with subsetting support (v1.1.6+)
- **Page Analysis**: Detect scanned vs text content with intelligent classification
- **OCR Integration**: Pluggable OCR support with Tesseract for processing scanned documents (v0.1.3+)
- **Resource Access**: Work with fonts, images, and other PDF resources
- **Pure Rust**: No C dependencies or external libraries
- **100% Native**: Complete PDF implementation from scratch

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

[§](https://docs.rs#creating-pdfs)Creating PDFs

```
use oxidize_pdf::{Document, Page, Font, Color, Result};
// Create a new document
let mut doc = Document::new();
doc.set_title("My PDF");
// Create a page
let mut page = Page::a4();
// Add text
page.text()
    .set_font(Font::Helvetica, 24.0)
    .at(50.0, 700.0)
    .write("Hello, PDF!")?;
// Add graphics
page.graphics()
    .set_fill_color(Color::rgb(0.0, 0.5, 1.0))
    .circle(300.0, 400.0, 50.0)
    .fill();
// Save the document
doc.add_page(page);
doc.save("output.pdf")?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-pdfs)Parsing PDFs

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
// Open and parse a PDF
let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
// Get document information
println!("Pages: {}", document.page_count()?);
println!("Version: {}", document.version()?);
// Process pages
for i in 0..document.page_count()? {
    let page = document.get_page(i)?;
    println!("Page {} size: {}x{} points", i+1, page.width(), page.height());
}
// Extract text
let text_pages = document.extract_text()?;
for (i, page_text) in text_pages.iter().enumerate() {
    println!("Page {} text: {}", i+1, page_text.text);
}
```

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#content-stream-processing)Content Stream Processing

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
use oxidize_pdf::parser::content::{ContentParser, ContentOperation};
let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
let page = document.get_page(0)?;
// Get and parse content streams
let streams = page.content_streams_with_document(&document)?;
for stream in streams {
    let operations = ContentParser::parse(&stream)?;

    for op in operations {
        match op {
            ContentOperation::ShowText(text) => {
                println!("Text: {:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&text));
            }
            ContentOperation::SetFont(name, size) => {
                println!("Font: {} at {} pt", name, size);
            }
            ContentOperation::MoveTo(x, y) => {
                println!("Move to ({}, {})", x, y);
            }
            _ => {} // Handle other operations
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#resource-access)Resource Access

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
let page = document.get_page(0)?;
// Access page resources
if let Some(resources) = page.get_resources() {
    // Check fonts
    if let Some(fonts) = resources.get("Font").and_then(|f| f.as_dict()) {
        for (name, _) in &fonts.0 {
            println!("Font resource: {}", name.as_str());
        }
    }

    // Check images/XObjects
    if let Some(xobjects) = resources.get("XObject").and_then(|x| x.as_dict()) {
        for (name, _) in &xobjects.0 {
            println!("XObject resource: {}", name.as_str());
        }
    }
}
```

# oxidize_pdf - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/oxidize_pdf/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#oxidize-pdf)oxidize-pdf

A comprehensive, pure Rust PDF library for generation, parsing, and manipulation with zero external PDF dependencies.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- **PDF Generation**: Create multi-page documents with text, graphics, and images
- **PDF Parsing**: Complete parser supporting rendering and content extraction
- **PDF Operations**: Split, merge, rotate, and extract pages
- **Text Extraction**: Extract text with position and formatting information
- **Image Extraction**: Extract images in JPEG, PNG, and TIFF formats
- **Font Embedding**: TrueType and OpenType font embedding with subsetting support (v1.1.6+)
- **Page Analysis**: Detect scanned vs text content with intelligent classification
- **OCR Integration**: Pluggable OCR support with Tesseract for processing scanned documents (v0.1.3+)
- **Resource Access**: Work with fonts, images, and other PDF resources
- **Pure Rust**: No C dependencies or external libraries
- **100% Native**: Complete PDF implementation from scratch

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

[§](https://docs.rs#creating-pdfs)Creating PDFs

```
use oxidize_pdf::{Document, Page, Font, Color, Result};
// Create a new document
let mut doc = Document::new();
doc.set_title("My PDF");
// Create a page
let mut page = Page::a4();
// Add text
page.text()
    .set_font(Font::Helvetica, 24.0)
    .at(50.0, 700.0)
    .write("Hello, PDF!")?;
// Add graphics
page.graphics()
    .set_fill_color(Color::rgb(0.0, 0.5, 1.0))
    .circle(300.0, 400.0, 50.0)
    .fill();
// Save the document
doc.add_page(page);
doc.save("output.pdf")?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-pdfs)Parsing PDFs

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
// Open and parse a PDF
let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
// Get document information
println!("Pages: {}", document.page_count()?);
println!("Version: {}", document.version()?);
// Process pages
for i in 0..document.page_count()? {
    let page = document.get_page(i)?;
    println!("Page {} size: {}x{} points", i+1, page.width(), page.height());
}
// Extract text
let text_pages = document.extract_text()?;
for (i, page_text) in text_pages.iter().enumerate() {
    println!("Page {} text: {}", i+1, page_text.text);
}
```

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#content-stream-processing)Content Stream Processing

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
use oxidize_pdf::parser::content::{ContentParser, ContentOperation};
let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
let page = document.get_page(0)?;
// Get and parse content streams
let streams = page.content_streams_with_document(&document)?;
for stream in streams {
    let operations = ContentParser::parse(&stream)?;

    for op in operations {
        match op {
            ContentOperation::ShowText(text) => {
                println!("Text: {:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&text));
            }
            ContentOperation::SetFont(name, size) => {
                println!("Font: {} at {} pt", name, size);
            }
            ContentOperation::MoveTo(x, y) => {
                println!("Move to ({}, {})", x, y);
            }
            _ => {} // Handle other operations
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#resource-access)Resource Access

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
let page = document.get_page(0)?;
// Access page resources
if let Some(resources) = page.get_resources() {
    // Check fonts
    if let Some(fonts) = resources.get("Font").and_then(|f| f.as_dict()) {
        for (name, _) in &fonts.0 {
            println!("Font resource: {}", name.as_str());
        }
    }

    // Check images/XObjects
    if let Some(xobjects) = resources.get("XObject").and_then(|x| x.as_dict()) {
        for (name, _) in &xobjects.0 {
            println!("XObject resource: {}", name.as_str());
        }
    }
}
```

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/src/oxidize_pdf/lib.rs.html

# oxidize_pdf/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! # oxidize-pdf
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! A comprehensive, pure Rust PDF library for generation, parsing, and manipulation with zero external PDF dependencies.
[4](https://docs.rs#4)
[5](https://docs.rs#5)#![allow(clippy::all)]
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//!
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! ## Features
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! - **PDF Generation**: Create multi-page documents with text, graphics, and images
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! - **PDF Parsing**: Complete parser supporting rendering and content extraction
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! - **PDF Operations**: Split, merge, rotate, and extract pages
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! - **Text Extraction**: Extract text with position and formatting information
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! - **Image Extraction**: Extract images in JPEG, PNG, and TIFF formats
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! - **Font Embedding**: TrueType and OpenType font embedding with subsetting support (v1.1.6+)
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! - **Page Analysis**: Detect scanned vs text content with intelligent classification
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! - **OCR Integration**: Pluggable OCR support with Tesseract for processing scanned documents (v0.1.3+)
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! - **Resource Access**: Work with fonts, images, and other PDF resources
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! - **Pure Rust**: No C dependencies or external libraries
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! - **100% Native**: Complete PDF implementation from scratch
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! ## Quick Start
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! ### Creating PDFs
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! ```rust
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! use oxidize_pdf::{Document, Page, Font, Color, Result};
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//!
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! # fn main() -> Result<()> {
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! // Create a new document
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! let mut doc = Document::new();
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! doc.set_title("My PDF");
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! // Create a page
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! let mut page = Page::a4();
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! // Add text
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! page.text()
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!     .set_font(Font::Helvetica, 24.0)
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!     .at(50.0, 700.0)
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!     .write("Hello, PDF!")?;
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! // Add graphics
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! page.graphics()
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!     .set_fill_color(Color::rgb(0.0, 0.5, 1.0))
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!     .circle(300.0, 400.0, 50.0)
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!     .fill();
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! // Save the document
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! doc.add_page(page);
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! doc.save("output.pdf")?;
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! # Ok(())
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! # }
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! ```
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//!
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! ### Parsing PDFs
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//!
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! ```rust,no_run
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! # fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! // Open and parse a PDF
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! // Get document information
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! println!("Pages: {}", document.page_count()?);
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! println!("Version: {}", document.version()?);
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! // Process pages
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! for i in 0..document.page_count()? {
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!     let page = document.get_page(i)?;
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!     println!("Page {} size: {}x{} points", i+1, page.width(), page.height());
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! }
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! // Extract text
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! let text_pages = document.extract_text()?;
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! for (i, page_text) in text_pages.iter().enumerate() {
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//!     println!("Page {} text: {}", i+1, page_text.text);
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! }
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! # Ok(())
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! # }
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! ```
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//!
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! ## Modules
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! ### Generation Modules
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! - [`document`] - PDF document creation and management
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! - [`page`] - Page creation and layout
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! - [`graphics`] - Vector graphics and images
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! - [`text`] - Text rendering and flow
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! - [`writer`] - Low-level PDF writing
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! ### Parsing Modules
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//! - [`parser`] - Complete PDF parsing and reading
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!   - [`parser::PdfDocument`] - High-level document interface
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//!   - [`parser::ParsedPage`] - Page representation with resources
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//!   - [`parser::ContentParser`] - Content stream parsing
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!   - [`parser::PdfObject`] - Low-level PDF objects
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//!
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! ### Manipulation Modules
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! - [`operations`] - PDF manipulation (split, merge, rotate, extract images)
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! - [`operations::page_analysis`] - Page content analysis and scanned page detection
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! - [`text::extraction`] - Text extraction with positioning
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//!
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! ### OCR Modules (v0.1.3+)
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//! - [`text::ocr`] - OCR trait system and types
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! - [`text::tesseract_provider`] - Tesseract OCR provider (requires `ocr-tesseract` feature)
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! - [`text::ocr`] - OCR integration for scanned documents
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//!
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//! ## Examples
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//!
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! ### Content Stream Processing
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//!
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//! ```rust,no_run
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//! use oxidize_pdf::parser::content::{ContentParser, ContentOperation};
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//!
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//! # fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//! let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//! let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//! let page = document.get_page(0)?;
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//!
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//! // Get and parse content streams
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//! let streams = page.content_streams_with_document(&document)?;
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//! for stream in streams {
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//!     let operations = ContentParser::parse(&stream)?;
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//!
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//!     for op in operations {
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//!         match op {
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//!             ContentOperation::ShowText(text) => {
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//!                 println!("Text: {:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&text));
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//!             }
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//!             ContentOperation::SetFont(name, size) => {
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//!                 println!("Font: {} at {} pt", name, size);
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//!             }
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//!             ContentOperation::MoveTo(x, y) => {
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//!                 println!("Move to ({}, {})", x, y);
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//!             }
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//!             _ => {} // Handle other operations
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//!         }
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//!     }
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//! }
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//! # Ok(())
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//! # }
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//! ```
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//!
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//! ### Resource Access
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//!
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//! ```rust,no_run
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//! use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//!
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//! # fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//! let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//! let page = document.get_page(0)?;
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//!
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//! // Access page resources
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//! if let Some(resources) = page.get_resources() {
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//!     // Check fonts
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//!     if let Some(fonts) = resources.get("Font").and_then(|f| f.as_dict()) {
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//!         for (name, _) in &fonts.0 {
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//!             println!("Font resource: {}", name.as_str());
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//!         }
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!     }
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//!
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//!     // Check images/XObjects
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//!     if let Some(xobjects) = resources.get("XObject").and_then(|x| x.as_dict()) {
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//!         for (name, _) in &xobjects.0 {
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!             println!("XObject resource: {}", name.as_str());
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//!         }
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//!     }
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//! }
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//! # Ok(())
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//! # }
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//! ```

[438](https://docs.rs#438)///

[441](https://docs.rs#441)/// used_glyphs.insert(65); // 'A'
[442](https://docs.rs#442)/// used_glyphs.insert(66); // 'B'

[444](https://docs.rs#444)///

[447](https://docs.rs#447)///     subset: true,                    // Create font subset
[448](https://docs.rs#448)///     compress_font_streams: true,     // Compress font data
[449](https://docs.rs#449)///     ..Default::default()
[450](https://docs.rs#450)/// };

[455](https://docs.rs#455)/// // Embed the font

# oxidize_pdf::parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/oxidize_pdf/parser/index.html

## Expand description

PDF Parser Module - Complete PDF parsing and rendering support

This module provides a comprehensive, 100% native Rust implementation for parsing PDF files according to the ISO 32000-1 (PDF 1.7) and ISO 32000-2 (PDF 2.0) specifications.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

The parser is designed to support building PDF renderers, content extractors, and analysis tools. It provides multiple levels of API access:

- **High-level**:- `PdfDocument`for easy document manipulation
- **Mid-level**:- `ParsedPage`, content streams, and resources
- **Low-level**: Direct access to PDF objects and streams

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
use oxidize_pdf::parser::content::ContentParser;
// Open a PDF document
let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
// Get document information
println!("Pages: {}", document.page_count()?);
println!("Version: {}", document.version()?);
// Process first page
let page = document.get_page(0)?;
println!("Page size: {}x{} points", page.width(), page.height());
// Parse content streams
let streams = page.content_streams_with_document(&document)?;
for stream in streams {
    let operations = ContentParser::parse(&stream)?;
    println!("Operations: {}", operations.len());
}
// Extract text
let text = document.extract_text_from_page(0)?;
println!("Text: {}", text.text);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 PdfDocument                     │ ← High-level API
│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────────────┐  │
│  │PdfReader │ │PageTree  │ │ResourceManager │  │
│  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           │              │              │
           ↓              ↓              ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              ParsedPage                         │ ← Page API
│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────────────┐  │
│  │Properties│ │Resources │ │Content Streams │  │
│  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           │              │              │
           ↓              ↓              ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         ContentParser & PdfObject               │ ← Low-level API
│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────────────┐  │
│  │Tokenizer │ │Operators │ │Object Types    │  │
│  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- **Complete PDF Object Model**: All PDF object types supported
- **Content Stream Parsing**: Full operator support for rendering
- **Resource Management**: Fonts, images, color spaces, patterns
- **Text Extraction**: With position and formatting information
- **Page Navigation**: Efficient page tree traversal
- **Stream Filters**: Decompression support (FlateDecode, ASCIIHex, etc.)
- **Reference Resolution**: Automatic handling of indirect objects

[§](https://docs.rs#example-building-a-simple-renderer)Example: Building a Simple Renderer

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
use oxidize_pdf::parser::content::{ContentParser, ContentOperation};
struct SimpleRenderer {
    current_path: Vec<(f32, f32)>,
}
impl SimpleRenderer {
    fn render_page(document: &PdfDocument<std::fs::File>, page_idx: u32) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
        let page = document.get_page(page_idx)?;
        let streams = page.content_streams_with_document(&document)?;

        let mut renderer = SimpleRenderer {
            current_path: Vec::new(),
        };

        for stream in streams {
            let operations = ContentParser::parse(&stream)?;
            for op in operations {
                match op {
                    ContentOperation::MoveTo(x, y) => {
                        renderer.current_path.clear();
                        renderer.current_path.push((x, y));
                    }
                    ContentOperation::LineTo(x, y) => {
                        renderer.current_path.push((x, y));
                    }
                    ContentOperation::Stroke => {
                        println!("Draw path with {} points", renderer.current_path.len());
                        renderer.current_path.clear();
                    }
                    ContentOperation::ShowText(text) => {
                        println!("Draw text: {:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&text));
                    }
                    _ => {} // Handle other operations
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

# PdfDocument in oxidize_pdf::parser::document - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/oxidize_pdf/parser/document/struct.PdfDocument.html

## Expand description

High-level PDF document interface for parsing and manipulation.

`PdfDocument` provides a clean, safe API for working with PDF files.
It handles the complexity of PDF structure, object references, and resource
management behind a simple interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#type-parameter)Type Parameter

- `R`- The reader type (must implement Read + Seek)

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture-benefits)Architecture Benefits

- **RefCell Usage**: Allows multiple parts of the API to access the document
- **Lazy Loading**: Pages and resources are loaded on demand
- **Automatic Caching**: Frequently accessed objects are cached
- **Safe API**: Borrow checker issues are handled internally

[§](https://docs.rs#thread-safety)Thread Safety

`PdfDocument<R>` is `Send` for `R: Send` (issue #369): it can be moved to
another thread or across a Python GIL boundary (e.g. `Python::allow_threads`).
It is intentionally `!Sync` because `RefCell` does not permit shared concurrent
access; callers that need concurrent reads should use one instance per thread.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
use std::fs::File;
// From a file
let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
// From any Read + Seek source
let file = File::open("document.pdf")?;
let reader = PdfReader::new(file)?;
let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
// Use the document
let page_count = document.page_count()?;
for i in 0..page_count {
    let page = document.get_page(i)?;
    // Process page...
}
```

- Required page properties are missing

#### pub fn [get_object](https://docs.rs#method.get_object)(&self, obj_num: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html), gen_num: [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)) -> [ParseResult](https://docs.rs/type.ParseResult.html)<[PdfObject](https://docs.rs/objects/enum.PdfObject.html)>

Get an object by its reference numbers.

This method first checks the cache, then loads from the file if needed. Objects are automatically cached after loading.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-1)Arguments

- `obj_num`- Object number
- `gen_num`- Generation number

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-4)Returns

The resolved PDF object.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-2)Errors

Returns an error if:

- Object doesn’t exist
- Object is part of an encrypted object stream
- File is corrupted

[§](https://docs.rs#example-5)Example

```
// Get object 10 0 R
let obj = document.get_object(10, 0)?;
// Check object type
match obj {
    PdfObject::Dictionary(dict) => {
        println!("Object is a dictionary with {} entries", dict.0.len());
    }
    PdfObject::Stream(stream) => {
        println!("Object is a stream");
    }
    _ => {}
}
```

#### pub fn [resolve](https://docs.rs#method.resolve)(&self, obj: &[PdfObject](https://docs.rs/objects/enum.PdfObject.html)) -> [ParseResult](https://docs.rs/type.ParseResult.html)<[PdfObject](https://docs.rs/objects/enum.PdfObject.html)>

Resolve a reference to get the actual object.

If the input is a Reference, fetches the referenced object. Otherwise returns a clone of the input object.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-2)Arguments

- `obj`- The object to resolve (may be a Reference or direct object)

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-5)Returns

The resolved object (never a Reference).

[§](https://docs.rs#example-6)Example

```
// Contents might be a reference or direct object
if let Some(contents) = page.dict.get("Contents") {
    let resolved = document.resolve(contents)?;
    match resolved {
        PdfObject::Stream(_) => println!("Single content stream"),
        PdfObject::Array(_) => println!("Multiple content streams"),
        _ => println!("Unexpected content type"),
    }
}
```

Build RAG chunks stamped with source-document metadata.

Auto-fills `title`/`author`/`creation_date`/`total_pages` from the info
dictionary (only where the caller left them `None`); the caller-supplied
`source` provides `filename`/`doc_hash` (and may override any auto-filled
field). `doc_hash`, when set, becomes the stable prefix of every
`chunk_id`. Same chunking pipeline as [ rag_chunks](https://docs.rs/struct.PdfDocument.html#method.rag_chunks).

[§](https://docs.rs#example-17)Example

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::PdfDocument;
use oxidize_pdf::pipeline::DocumentSource;
let doc = PdfDocument::open("document.pdf")?;
let mut source = DocumentSource::default();
source.filename = Some("document.pdf".to_string());
source.doc_hash = Some("sha256-prefix".to_string());
let chunks = doc.rag_chunks_with_source(source)?;

Partition the document into typed elements and build a relationship graph.

Returns a tuple of `(elements, graph)` where the graph captures parent/child
and next/prev relationships between elements by index.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-21)Example

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::PdfDocument;
use oxidize_pdf::pipeline::PartitionConfig;
let doc = PdfDocument::open("document.pdf")?;
let (elements, graph) = doc.partition_graph(PartitionConfig::default())?;
for title_idx in graph.top_level_sections() {
    println!("Section: {}", elements[title_idx].text());
    for child_idx in graph.elements_in_section(title_idx) {
        println!("  {}", elements[child_idx].text());
    }
}
```

}## Expand description

Represents a single page in the PDF with all its properties and resources.

A `ParsedPage` contains all the information needed to render or analyze a PDF page,
including its dimensions, content streams, resources, and inherited properties from
parent page tree nodes.

[§](https://docs.rs#fields-1)Fields

- `obj_ref`- Object reference (object number, generation number) pointing to this page in the PDF
- `dict`- Complete page dictionary containing all page-specific entries
- `inherited_resources`- Resources inherited from parent page tree nodes
- `media_box`- Page dimensions in PDF units [llx, lly, urx, ury]
- `crop_box`- Optional visible area of the page
- `rotation`- Page rotation in degrees (0, 90, 180, or 270)

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::{PdfDocument, PdfReader};
let reader = PdfReader::open("document.pdf")?;
let document = PdfDocument::new(reader);
let page = document.get_page(0)?;
// Access page properties
let (obj_num, gen_num) = page.obj_ref;
println!("Page object: {} {} R", obj_num, gen_num);
// Get page dimensions
let [llx, lly, urx, ury] = page.media_box;
println!("MediaBox: ({}, {}) to ({}, {})", llx, lly, urx, ury);
// Check for content
if let Some(contents) = page.dict.get("Contents") {
    println!("Page has content streams");
}
```
## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

`media_box: [`[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html); [4](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]MediaBox defining the page dimensions in PDF units (typically points). Format: [lower_left_x, lower_left_y, upper_right_x, upper_right_y]

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.crop_box)

If None, the entire MediaBox is visible.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.rotation)

`rotation: `[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)Page rotation in degrees. Valid values are 0, 90, 180, or 270. The rotation is applied clockwise.

Get the effective page width accounting for rotation.

The width is calculated from the MediaBox and adjusted based on the page rotation. For 90° or 270° rotations, the width and height are swapped.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

The page width in PDF units (typically points, where 1 point = 1/72 inch)

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
let page = document.get_page(0)?;
let width_pts = page.width();
let width_inches = width_pts / 72.0;
let width_mm = width_pts * 25.4 / 72.0;
println!("Page width: {} points ({:.2} inches, {:.2} mm)", width_pts, width_inches, width_mm);
```
Get the effective page height accounting for rotation.

The height is calculated from the MediaBox and adjusted based on the page rotation. For 90° or 270° rotations, the width and height are swapped.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-1)Returns

Get the content streams for this page using a PdfReader.

Content streams contain the actual drawing instructions (operators) that render text, graphics, and images on the page. A page may have multiple content streams which are concatenated during rendering.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `reader`- Mutable reference to the PDF reader

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-2)Returns

A vector of decompressed content stream data. Each vector contains the raw bytes of a content stream ready for parsing.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns an error if:

- The Contents entry is malformed
- Stream decompression fails
- Referenced objects cannot be resolved

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

```
let streams = page.content_streams(reader)?;
for (i, stream) in streams.iter().enumerate() {
    println!("Content stream {}: {} bytes", i, stream.len());
}
```

Get the effective resources for this page (including inherited).

Resources include fonts, images (XObjects), color spaces, patterns, and other assets needed to render the page. This method returns page-specific resources if present, otherwise falls back to inherited resources from parent nodes.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-4)Returns

The Resources dictionary if available, or None if the page has no resources.

[§](https://docs.rs#resource-categories)Resource Categories

The Resources dictionary may contain:

- `Font`- Font definitions used by text operators
- `XObject`- External objects (images, form XObjects)
- `ColorSpace`- Color space definitions
- `Pattern`- Pattern definitions for fills
- `Shading`- Shading dictionaries
- `ExtGState`- Graphics state parameter dictionaries
- `Properties`- Property list dictionaries

[§](https://docs.rs#example-5)Example

```
if let Some(resources) = page.get_resources() {
    // Check for fonts
    if let Some(fonts) = resources.get("Font").and_then(|f| f.as_dict()) {
        println!("Page uses {} fonts", fonts.0.len());
    }

    // Check for images
    if let Some(xobjects) = resources.get("XObject").and_then(|x| x.as_dict()) {
        println!("Page has {} XObjects", xobjects.0.len());
    }
}
```

Get all objects referenced by this page (for extraction or analysis).

This method recursively collects all objects referenced by the page, including:

- Content streams
- Resources (fonts, images, etc.)
- Nested objects within resources

This is useful for extracting a complete page with all its dependencies or for analyzing the object graph of a page.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-2)Arguments

- `reader`- Mutable reference to the PDF reader

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-7)Returns

A HashMap mapping object references (obj_num, gen_num) to their resolved objects.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-9)Example

```
let referenced_objects = page.get_referenced_objects(reader)?;
println!("Page references {} objects", referenced_objects.len());
for ((obj_num, gen_num), obj) in &referenced_objects {
    println!("  {} {} R: {:?}", obj_num, gen_num, obj);
}
```

# ContentParser in oxidize_pdf::parser::content - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/oxidize_pdf/parser/content/struct.ContentParser.html

`pub struct ContentParser { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

High-level content stream parser.

Converts tokenized content streams into structured `ContentOperation` values.
This parser handles the operand stack and operator parsing according to PDF specifications.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The parser is typically used through its static methods:

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::content::ContentParser;
let content = b"q 1 0 0 1 50 50 cm 100 100 200 150 re S Q";
let operations = ContentParser::parse(content)?;
```

Parse a content stream into a vector of operators.

This is a convenience method that creates a parser and processes the entire stream.

- `content`- Raw content stream bytes (may be compressed)

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

A vector of parsed `ContentOperation` values in the order they appear.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns an error if:

- Invalid operator syntax is encountered
- Operators have incorrect number/type of operands
- Unknown operators are found

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```

let operations = ContentParser::parse(content)?;

assert!(matches!(operations[0], ContentOperation::BeginText));
```

# PdfObject in oxidize_pdf::parser::objects - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/oxidize_pdf/parser/objects/enum.PdfObject.html

```
pub enum PdfObject {
    Null,
    Boolean(
```
[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)),
    Integer([i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)),
    Real([f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)),
    String([PdfString](https://docs.rs/struct.PdfString.html)),
    Name([PdfName](https://docs.rs/struct.PdfName.html)),
    Array([PdfArray](https://docs.rs/struct.PdfArray.html)),
    Dictionary([PdfDictionary](https://docs.rs/struct.PdfDictionary.html)),
    Stream([PdfStream](https://docs.rs/struct.PdfStream.html)),
    Reference([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html), [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)),
}## Expand description

PDF Object types - The fundamental data types in PDF.

All data in a PDF file is represented using these basic types. Objects can be direct (embedded) or indirect (referenced).

[§](https://docs.rs#object-types)Object Types

- `Null`- Undefined/absent value
- `Boolean`- true or false
- `Integer`- Signed integers
- `Real`- Floating-point numbers
- `String`- Text or binary data
- `Name`- Atomic symbols like /Type
- `Array`- Ordered collections
- `Dictionary`- Key-value maps
- `Stream`- Dictionary + binary data
- `Reference`- Indirect object reference (num gen R)

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use oxidize_pdf::parser::objects::{PdfObject, PdfName, PdfString};
// Different object types
let null = PdfObject::Null;
let bool_val = PdfObject::Boolean(true);
let int_val = PdfObject::Integer(42);
let real_val = PdfObject::Real(3.14159);
let name = PdfObject::Name(PdfName::new("Type".to_string()));
let reference = PdfObject::Reference(10, 0); // 10 0 R
// Type checking
assert!(int_val.as_integer().is_some());
assert_eq!(int_val.as_integer(), Some(42));
```

Parse a PDF object from a lexer.

Reads tokens from the lexer and constructs the appropriate PDF object. Handles all PDF object types including indirect references.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

The parsed PDF object.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

- Unexpected end of input
- Malformed object structure

use oxidize_pdf::parser::lexer::Lexer;
use oxidize_pdf::parser::objects::PdfObject;

let input = b"42";

# oxidize_pdf::operations::page_analysis - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/oxidize_pdf/operations/page_analysis/index.html

## Expand description

PDF page content analysis

This module provides functionality to analyze the content composition of PDF pages, helping to determine whether pages contain primarily scanned images, vector text, or a mixture of both. This is particularly useful for:

- Detecting scanned documents that may benefit from OCR processing
- Analyzing document composition for optimization purposes
- Preprocessing documents for different handling strategies

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use oxidize_pdf::operations::page_analysis::{PageContentAnalyzer, PageType};
use oxidize_pdf::parser::PdfReader;
let document = PdfReader::open_document("example.pdf")?;
let analyzer = PageContentAnalyzer::new(document);
// Analyze a specific page
let analysis = analyzer.analyze_page(0)?;
match analysis.page_type {
    PageType::Scanned => println!("This page appears to be scanned"),
    PageType::Text => println!("This page contains primarily vector text"),
    PageType::Mixed => println!("This page contains both text and images"),
}
// Quick check for scanned pages
if analyzer.is_scanned_page(0)? {
    println!("Page 0 is likely a scanned image");
}
```

- Configuration options for page content analysis

- Analyzer for PDF page content composition

# oxidize_pdf::text::ocr - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/oxidize_pdf/text/ocr/index.html

## Expand description

OCR (Optical Character Recognition) support for PDF processing

This module provides a flexible, pluggable architecture for integrating OCR capabilities into PDF processing workflows. It’s designed to work seamlessly with the page analysis module to process scanned pages and extract text from images.

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

The OCR system uses a trait-based approach that allows for multiple OCR providers:

- **OcrProvider trait**: Generic interface for OCR engines
- **Pluggable implementations**: Support for local (Tesseract) and cloud (Azure, AWS) providers
- **Result standardization**: Consistent output format regardless of provider
- **Error handling**: Comprehensive error types for OCR operations

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#basic-ocr-processing)Basic OCR Processing

```
use oxidize_pdf::text::{MockOcrProvider, OcrOptions, OcrProvider};
use oxidize_pdf::graphics::ImageFormat;
let provider = MockOcrProvider::new();
let options = OcrOptions::default();
// Process image data directly - Mock JPEG data
let image_data = vec![
    0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xE0, 0x00, 0x10, 0x4A, 0x46, 0x49, 0x46, 0x00, 0x01,
    0x01, 0x01, 0x00, 0x48, 0x00, 0x48, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0xD9
];
let result = provider.process_image(&image_data, &options)?;
println!("Extracted text: {}", result.text);
println!("Confidence: {:.2}%", result.confidence * 100.0);
for fragment in result.fragments {
    println!("Fragment: '{}' at ({}, {})", fragment.text, fragment.x, fragment.y);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#integration-with-page-analysis)Integration with Page Analysis

```
use oxidize_pdf::operations::page_analysis::PageContentAnalyzer;
use oxidize_pdf::text::{MockOcrProvider, OcrOptions};
use oxidize_pdf::parser::PdfReader;
let document = PdfReader::open_document("scanned.pdf")?;
let analyzer = PageContentAnalyzer::new(document);
let provider = MockOcrProvider::new();
// Find scanned pages
let scanned_pages = analyzer.find_scanned_pages()?;
for page_num in scanned_pages {
    let analysis = analyzer.analyze_page(page_num)?;
    if analysis.is_scanned() {
        println!("Processing scanned page {}", page_num);
        // OCR processing would happen here
    }
}
```

# TransformMatrix in oxidize_pdf::coordinate_system - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/oxidize_pdf/coordinate_system/struct.TransformMatrix.html

```
pub struct TransformMatrix {
    pub a:
```
[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    pub b: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    pub c: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    pub d: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    pub e: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    pub f: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
}## Expand description

2D transformation matrix in homogeneous coordinates

Represents a 3x3 matrix in the form:

```
[a c e]   [x]     [ax + cy + e]
[b d f] × [y]  =  [bx + dy + f]
[0 0 1]   [1]     [    1      ]
```
Where `[x]`, `[y]`, and `[1]` represent the input vector.

Common transformations:

- Identity: `a=1, b=0, c=0, d=1, e=0, f=0`
- Translation: `a=1, b=0, c=0, d=1, e=tx, f=ty`
- Scale: `a=sx, b=0, c=0, d=sy, e=0, f=0`
- Y-flip: `a=1, b=0, c=0, d=-1, e=0, f=page_height`

# Document in oxidize_pdf::document - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/oxidize-pdf/3.0.5/oxidize_pdf/document/struct.Document.html

`pub struct Document { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A PDF document that can contain multiple pages and metadata.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use oxidize_pdf::{Document, Page};
let mut doc = Document::new();
doc.set_title("My Document");
doc.set_author("John Doe");
let page = Page::a4();
doc.add_page(page);
doc.save("output.pdf").unwrap();
```

#### pub fn [set_struct_tree](https://docs.rs#method.set_struct_tree)(&mut self, tree: [StructTree](https://docs.rs/structure/struct.StructTree.html))

Set the document structure tree for Tagged PDF (accessibility)

Tagged PDF provides semantic information about document content, making PDFs accessible to screen readers and assistive technologies.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
use oxidize_pdf::{Document, structure::{StructTree, StructureElement, StandardStructureType}};
let mut doc = Document::new();
let mut tree = StructTree::new();
// Create document root
let doc_elem = StructureElement::new(StandardStructureType::Document);
let doc_idx = tree.set_root(doc_elem);
// Add heading
let h1 = StructureElement::new(StandardStructureType::H1)
    .with_language("en-US")
    .with_actual_text("Welcome");
tree.add_child(doc_idx, h1).unwrap();
doc.set_struct_tree(tree);
```

`crate::fonts::Font::missing_glyphs`Characters in `text` that the named custom font cannot render because

    &mut self,
    name: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    data: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>,
    mapping: [CidMapping](https://docs.rs/fonts/cid_mapper/struct.CidMapping.html),

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/oxidize_pdf/document.rs.html#571-590)

#### pub fn [add_cid_keyed_font](https://docs.rs#method.add_cid_keyed_font)(
    &mut self,
    name: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    data: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>,
    mapping: [CidMapping](https://docs.rs/fonts/cid_mapper/struct.CidMapping.html),
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)>

Register a CID-keyed font for positioned-glyph-run drawing (issue #358).

Unlike [ add_font_from_bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Document.html#method.add_font_from_bytes) (which is
Unicode-keyed: content-stream codes are interpreted as Unicode code
points), a CID-keyed font interprets the 2-byte codes drawn via

[as the CIDs in](crate::text::TextContext::show_cid_array)

`show_cid_array``mapping`. With `CIDToGIDMap = Identity` (CID = GID) this lets a
caller draw a pre-shaped glyph run (e.g. from `rustybuzz`) directly by
glyph id, expressing ligatures and per-glyph positioning the
Unicode-keyed path cannot.`mapping` must carry `cid_to_gid` (which GID each CID renders) and
`cid_to_unicode` (so the text stays extractable via the emitted
`ToUnicode` CMap). The font is embedded whole — no subsetting in this
iteration. Registered separately from custom fonts so the two drawing
modes never share a font object.

Only TrueType/SFNT fonts (`CIDFontType2`) are supported in this
iteration; an OpenType/CFF font returns an error.

Gets a reference to the page at `index`, or `None` if out of bounds.

Gets a mutable reference to the page at `index`, or `None` if out of bounds.

Gets a reference to the AcroForm (interactive form) if present.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/oxidize_pdf/document.rs.html#647-650)#### pub fn [disable_forms](https://docs.rs#method.disable_forms)(&mut self)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/oxidize_pdf/document.rs.html#647-650)

#### pub fn [disable_forms](https://docs.rs#method.disable_forms)(&mut self)

Disables interactive forms by removing both the AcroForm and FormManager.

Fill an AcroForm field by name, updating `/V` and regenerating the
widget appearance stream(s) so the value is both machine-readable
(via `/V` on the field dictionary) and visually present in the PDF
(via `/AP/N` on each widget annotation).

This implements ISO 32000-1 §12.7.3.3 Table 228 (`/V` on form fields)
plus §12.5.5 / §12.7.3.3 interplay: a viewer that honours
`/NeedAppearances true` may regenerate appearance streams on open,
but a compliant writer should still emit them so the PDF renders
correctly in readers that do not.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `name`— the partial field name (- `/T`on the field dictionary) assigned when the field was registered via- `FormManager::add_*`.
- `value`— the new value. For text fields this becomes- `/V`as a PDF string; it is also embedded verbatim into the regenerated appearance content stream (see- `TextFieldAppearance`).

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

- `PdfError::InvalidStructure`if the document has no- `FormManager`attached (calling code must register fields before filling them).
- `PdfError::FieldNotFound`if no field with the given- `name`exists in the- `FormManager`.

[§](https://docs.rs#custom-type0cid-font-dispatch-issue-212)Custom Type0/CID font dispatch (issue #212)

Both `FieldType::Text` (TextField) and `FieldType::Choice` (ComboBox)
honour the field’s typed `/DA` and dispatch to the correct emission
path:

- `Font::Custom(name)`with the font registered via- `add_font_from_bytes`→ Type0/CID path. Hex-CID- `<HHHH> Tj`in the appearance content stream and a- `/Subtype /Type0`/- `/Encoding /Identity-H`resource entry that the writer rewrites to an indirect Reference to the document-level CIDFontType0 object.
- Built-in font (Helvetica, Times, Courier) → WinAnsi-strict path.
Returns `PdfError::EncodingError`for any character outside the WinAnsi repertoire.
- No `/DA`→ Helvetica fallback, same WinAnsi-strict path.

To use a custom font with a ComboBox, call
`ComboBox::with_default_appearance(Font::Custom("name"), size, color)`
before passing it to `FormManager::add_combo_box`. The same
constructor on `TextField` covers text fields. For PushButton labels
with custom fonts the resource dict is correct (Type0 placeholder)
but the label-render block is currently skipped; full hex-CID Tj for
push button labels remains a follow-up.

[§](https://docs.rs#path-chosen-v256-task-3)Path chosen (v2.5.6 Task 3)

This method operates on an in-memory `Document` that was BUILT in
the current process (via `FormManager` + `Page::add_form_widget_with_ref`).
It does not re-parse an existing PDF; hydration of a parsed PDF
back into a mutable `Document` is out of scope for v2.5.6 Task 3
and tracked separately. The writer accepts the mutated document
and emits /V + /AP/N so the typical round-trip
“build → fill → save → reader sees filled value” is covered.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/oxidize_pdf/document.rs.html#1053-1055)#### pub fn [set_compress](https://docs.rs#method.set_compress)(&mut self, compress: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/oxidize_pdf/document.rs.html#1053-1055)

#### pub fn [set_compress](https://docs.rs#method.set_compress)(&mut self, compress: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Enables or disables compression for PDF streams.

When compression is enabled (default), content streams and XRef streams are compressed using Flate/Zlib compression to reduce file size. When disabled, streams are written uncompressed, making the PDF larger but easier to debug.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-2)Arguments

- `compress`- Whether to enable compression

[§](https://docs.rs#example-6)Example

```
use oxidize_pdf::{Document, Page};
let mut doc = Document::new();
// Disable compression for debugging
doc.set_compress(false);
doc.set_title("My Document");
doc.add_page(Page::a4());
let pdf_bytes = doc.to_bytes().unwrap();
println!("Uncompressed PDF size: {} bytes", pdf_bytes.len());
```

Enable or disable compressed cross-reference streams (PDF 1.5+).

Cross-reference streams provide more compact representation of the cross-reference table and support additional features like compressed object streams.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-7)Example

```
Generates the PDF document as bytes in memory.

This method provides in-memory PDF generation without requiring file I/O.
The document is serialized to bytes and returned as a `Vec<u8>`.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-1)Returns

Returns the PDF document as bytes on success.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-5)Errors

Returns an error if the document cannot be serialized.

```
use oxidize_pdf::{Document, Page};
let mut doc = Document::new();
doc.set_title("My Document");
let page = Page::a4();
doc.add_page(page);
let pdf_bytes = doc.to_bytes().unwrap();
println!("Generated PDF size: {} bytes", pdf_bytes.len());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/oxidize_pdf/document.rs.html#1178-1192)#### pub fn [to_bytes_with_config](https://docs.rs#method.to_bytes_with_config)(&mut self, config: [WriterConfig](https://docs.rs/writer/struct.WriterConfig.html)) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>>

#### pub fn [to_bytes_with_config](https://docs.rs#method.to_bytes_with_config)(&mut self, config: [WriterConfig](https://docs.rs/writer/struct.WriterConfig.html)) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>>

Generates the PDF document as bytes with custom writer configuration.

This method allows customizing the PDF output (e.g., using XRef streams) while still generating the document in memory.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-4)Arguments

- `config`- Writer configuration options

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-2)Returns

Returns the PDF document as bytes on success.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-6)Errors

Returns an error if the document cannot be serialized.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-9)Example

```
use oxidize_pdf::{Document, Page};
use oxidize_pdf::writer::WriterConfig;
let mut doc = Document::new();
doc.set_title("My Document");
let page = Page::a4();
doc.add_page(page);
let config = WriterConfig {
    use_xref_streams: true,
    use_object_streams: false,
    pdf_version: "1.5".to_string(),
    compress_streams: true,
    incremental_update: false,
};
let pdf_bytes = doc.to_bytes_with_config(config).unwrap();
println!("Generated PDF size: {} bytes", pdf_bytes.len());
```

Mark a region of the PDF with semantic meaning for AI processing.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-10)Example

```

    BoundingBox::new(100.0, 700.0, 150.0, 20.0, 1)
);

doc.add_entity_metadata(&entity_id, "confidence", "0.98");
